Needle meter for the first channel. In Reduce view it shows how many dB the gain is turned down. In Level view it shows the output level in dB.
Needle meter for the second channel. In Reduce view it shows how many dB the gain is turned down. In Level view it shows the output level in dB.

Input level (across) against output level (up). The bend is soft and gets steeper the harder you push, like a variable-mu tube stage. Amber is channel one, pink is channel two. The dashed line marks the threshold. The dot is the live signal.
How much each channel turned the signal down, over the last six seconds. Amber is channel one, pink is channel two.
Gain reduction in dB for this channel. More lights, more turned down. Numbers are dB.
Input sets how hard the signal hits the compressor, in 1 dB steps (0 to +24). More input means more gain reduction and more tube colour. Try: raise it 1 dB at a time until the needle moves 3 to 6 dB.

Threshold is the level where the box starts turning things down. At 0 only the loudest peaks are caught, higher numbers catch quieter sound too. Try: start at 2 and raise it until you see about 3 dB of gain reduction on the loud parts.
Time sets how fast the box grabs a loud sound (attack) and how slowly it lets go (release). Left is FAST and punchy, right is SLOW and smooth. Try: 2 for vocals and drums, 5 or 6 for a whole mix.
Four valves. The glow follows the gain reduction of each channel: two for channel one, two for channel two.
Left / Right treats the left and right sides as two channels. Try: use this for most sources.
Lat / Vert splits the sound into the middle (sum) and the sides (difference) and squeezes each on its own. Try: a master where the centre is too loud but the width is fine.
Link makes both channels turn down together, so the stereo picture does not lean to one side. Try: keep it on, turn it off only to set each channel separately.
Level Match keeps the processed sound as loud as the original so you judge the tone, not the volume. Try: switch it on, press Bypass (B) to compare, then switch it off.
Needle shows gain reduction: how many dB the gain is turned down.
Needle shows output level in dB.
Side-chain HP stops deep bass from triggering the squeeze, so the low end stays full. The sound itself is not filtered. Try: 120 Hz on a mix with a big kick.
Output is the volume after the squeeze, -12 to +12 dB. Try: raise it until the sound is as loud as before, so the compressor does not just sound louder.
Mix blends the original with the squeezed sound. 100 is all squeezed. Try: 40 to 50 on drums for punch with extra thickness.
Gain reduction in dB for this channel. More lights, more turned down. Numbers are dB.
